content:
The test image shows a soybean stem/pod junction with prominent **white, cottony mycelial growth** covering the tissue. The pod appears shriveled and dying, with fluffy white fungal growth — highly characteristic of White Mold. Background leaves are yellowing.

Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows late-stage White Mold with wilted/collapsed stems. The test image is an earlier/more active stage with visible white mycelium — the hallmark symptom of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*. The cottony white growth on the stem and pod is definitive.

This fluffy white mycelium is the hallmark symptom of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). No other soybean disease produces this characteristic white aerial mycelium on stems and pods."}
